english: My lord says this: give us the field of the river, or we come with spears. -- Does your lord threaten me? Say to your lord: our fathers held this field with us. Our young men are many and they do not fear. -- You are bold. War is bad (?) for the herds. -- Now let your lord come to me, and let us two speak. -- I will carry your words to him.
uncertain: kóryos stéh₂dʰh₁oybʰos h₂egʰṓd: no verb; h₂egʰṓd is ablative 'from the bad' - read as 'war is bad for the herds', which needs nominative h₂egʰós
ph₂téres nos ḱóm h₂éǵrom: ḱóm read as 'this' (acc.) or 'with'

english: From what people have you come here with a wagon? -- I have come from the far sea. -- Have you seen the sea? -- I have not seen it. -- What are you carrying? -- I carry salt and bronze. What will you give me? -- I will give you wool and skins. -- Is your wool good? Bring it to my wagon in the morning. -- I will bring it, and my sister will give her wool.
uncertain: 'came from the far sea' vs 'I have not seen the sea' looks contradictory; maybe 'from far, from beyond the sea'

english: I give you my son as a pledge. -- He will live in your household. -- Now I give you my brother's son too. Will you guard him? -- I will guard him, and he will eat with my sons. -- When will the two sons return home? -- Let them stay three winters. Then they will return home. -- If your people break the peace, your son will not return home. -- My people will not break it. I swear it by Father Sky.
uncertain: dual suHnúh₁ with 3pl nésōntor, but 3du ménētes

english: Husband, the other tribe has broken its pledge. They drove off our herds. -- I know it; the shepherds told me. -- What will you do? Will you go against them? -- I will send a man to them. If they give the herds back, there will be no war. -- And if they do not give them back? -- Then our young men will punish them, and Perkwunos will see it. Lady, are you afraid?

Old man, were the people of the river our enemies? -- They were our enemies. I remember the killing at the ford. Their men drove off our cattle and killed many of our men. -- Then why is there peace now? -- Our chief gave his own daughter to their chief. Now her children are kin, and they guard our herds. -- Will the peace stand? -- It will stand if men keep their oaths. Do you know this?
uncertain: h₁íh₂ ǵn̥néh₃si: 'do you know these things'

english: Lady, be well. I come from the king. -- Dear guest, sit and eat. Now hear my words. -- My lord's son seeks a wife. He wants your daughter. -- What bride-price will he give? -- He will give ten cows and a cup of gold. -- My daughter is dear to me. I will ask her. If she wants him, she will go with you.
uncertain: ḱóm + dative tébʰye (no pronoun instrumental in closed class)
speaker of 'sit and eat' presumably the lady
